utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Kearney, are you ready to continue your examination-in-chief? Perhaps I'll then first -- Witness 8, yesterday you have given a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Please be aware that this solemn declaration is still binding. Mr. Kearney, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness Number 8, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When we left off yesterday, you made the following statement, this is at page 91 of the transcript, line 22, you said yesterday that: "We were on a bus, I, my brother, and a friend. Isuf was near the door. I was behind. This person came there and said, You should come down because we have something to ask you about. And then they put them in a vehicle and I never saw them anymore." I want to ask you first: Do you remember testifying to that yesterday? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to now ask you some more questions about that statement, including this first one. Where were you, your friend, and your brother Isuf going on the bus that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Why were you going to Pristina that day, Witness Number 8, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were going to Pristina to do some shopping for myself and for my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you remember anything about what time of day it was? What time you left to go to Pristina that day? Was it day-time? Was it night-time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was day-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And where did your trip begin that day? Where were you leaving from on your way to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We started from Gjakove, and we proceeded to Malisheve and then to Prishtine. This was the shortest route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you told us yesterday that this -- this trip took place in 1998. I want to ask you if today you can remember when in 1998 this was. Do you remember what month it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know. I wouldn't lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you remember making a statement about this to the MUP back in 1998 -- I'm sorry, back in 2001, Witness Number 8?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who knew these things told me in detail, and we made this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you remember when you made the statement that -- this is to the MUP in 2001, that you mentioned this incident happened in May of 1998. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, the answer in relation to the person who knew these things, that's not entirely clear. Could you please seek clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 8, in your previous answer you mentioned that -- when I asked you about making a statement in 2001, you mentioned a person who knew these things. Who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person told me that this is what has happened, and you can proceed with this matter. You can take them to court, and I said to him that I'm determined to look for my family, to find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And with the Court's permission, I'm going to move on if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's still unclear to me, and it's, of course, a vital matter whether -- during that interview who had the information and who gave it to whom. That's a rather vital matter, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'll inquire further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 8, you mentioned that you talked with someone and they said that you can proceed with this matter, you can take them to court. And you mentioned to him: "I said to him that I'm determined to look for my family." First of all, who is it you're having this conversation with, if you can tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rame Karavata was his name. He was a refugee just like us. I asked him about these matters, and he said to me, You better make a statement and perhaps you can find your family. And I said that I will do my best to find my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When he suggested to you that you should make a statement, did you tell him about what happened on the bus or did he tell you what happened on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He knew. He was a kind of a leader, our leader. As I was without any education, I was not familiar with these proceedings, so I asked him what would be the best way to find my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And after you said that, did you tell -- did you tell Rame what you had seen and heard on the bus in Malisevo that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no need for me to tell him anything. That was something that had already happened. He just said to me, Take them to court and look for your family. Do your best to find them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, it's still not entirely clear. Witness 8, you said there was no need to tell him, but Rame had not seen it himself, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told him what had happened so that he could help me find my family. So he advised me to go to court, and I sought advice from him. I asked him what would be the best thing for me to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I want to ask you, Witness 8, you mentioned that there was -- besides your brother and yourself on the bus, there was a friend with you. Who was that friend?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What ethnicity was -- was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an Albanian married to a Serbian woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: At the time of this incident on the bus, what was his occupation, if you know, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was playing lottery with my brother. They were in each other's company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did your friend have a -- not your brother now. Did your friend have a job back then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not employed, so he was betting, playing lottery, just to make some money to provide for his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And how about your brother? Was he employed then? Did he have a job?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/08 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother was a tailor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, please tell us in more detail, if you could, about what happened when the bus got to Malisevo, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I stop you. First of all, I would like to have a redaction. Mr. Kearney, yesterday Mr. Emmerson drew our attention to perhaps the necessity of hearing quite a lot of the evidence in private session. I think what now happens demonstrates that it might be wiser. There's no application for closed session as a whole. At least I'd like to turn into private session now, and I'd like you to consider what's the appropriate way of proceeding.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness 8.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have been in court for a couple of hours. You've told us already a lot. You -- we observed that some matters are very much on your mind, whereas you found it difficult to answer or answer again other questions. The Chamber has decided that for the time being and since we have a week starting on from today that we are not sitting, that we'll not continue your examination as a witness. The Chamber will consider - and that might take quite some time - whether or not we'll continue at a later date. You've answered already all the questions of the Prosecution. There might be more questions from the Defence, there might be more questions from the Chamber, but it's also possible that we are satisfied for the time being with the testimony you have given until now. So therefore, I take it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I take it that the witness will return to the place where he resides? I take it that must have been planned anyhow?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, at this moment we'll not put further questions to you, and you'll be informed whether at a later stage we'd like to continue. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem with me. Whenever you call me, I will be ready. I will respond to your call immediately, but you should bear in mind that I'm a poor man. I'm only concerned about the children of my brother's son. I'm doing my best to provide for them. I search rubbish bins, whatever it takes, just to be able to secure a crust of bread for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber fully understands that you're living in circumstances which you describe as poor and not easy. Since there is a possibility that we would re-call you at a later stage, you're instructed not to speak with other persons about the testimony you have given or testimony you possibly will give in the future. Have you understood that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will not speak at all with anybody; however, I appeal to the Albanian people not to do me any harm because I'm all alone now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Human beings should not do any harm to each other. That is a -- that may be clear. I then will now ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom, and in case we might not see you again, I would like to thank you that you have come to The Hague and that you gave your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I agree with whatever you say. I don't have anything against your words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were with --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Should we return into private session or not? I don't know what's on your list remaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's one -- there's one matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You indicate when we have the need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think -- I think not, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The second was -- concerned the evidence of Zvonko Markovic and the statement of his brother Rade. That statement was neither exhibited nor marked for identification, and the matter was left at the end of his evidence on the basis that Mr. Di Fazio was to let me know whether the Prosecution was prepared to make a stipulation about the passage in the statement or whether the whole of the statement was to be exhibited. So that's something which needs to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So a response still to be expected from Mr. Di Fazio. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thirdly, the notebooks of Marijana Andjelkovic. My understanding had been that the Trial Chamber had directed the Prosecution to resurvey a complete set Marijana Andjelkovic's notebooks in proper translation and in proper order. And what I think the Prosecution has proposed is a selection from the translations that were in existence at the time that she gave evidence. What we need to have is a solid base from which to work of all of her notebooks, so that we know that we're using the same pagination and the same correct order, and then once we have that to be able to propose which passages from those notebooks should come before the Trial Chamber in terms of admitted evidence. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most important was that the matters would be re-arranged in such a way that it would avoid whatever confusion --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and that it would be unambiguous as to paging, translations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the Prosecution has jumped straight to the next stage and simply made some proposals of passages from the existing misordered translations unless I've misunderstood the position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would encourage -- I would encourage further contact between the parties to see whether they can sort it out; if not, then, of course, the Chamber will give a ruling on what steps that would be needed to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour asked for a response from us on that and our response is we stand ready to indicate which passages we would like exhibited and which ones we object to, as soon as we are clear that we have what the Prosecution says is the final translation of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I'm not pressing any response at this moment, but at least drawing your attention to the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I thought that what we put into e-court was the re-arranged ones, but I will certainly check. That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Try to -- try to communicate in such a way that you understand why Mr. Emmerson thinks that it's not the intended re-arranged material and why you think it is. And then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Next, item number 4, there were two exhibits left - if I may put it this way - floating, P30 and D30, and the question was should they be admitted under seal or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: P30, as we understand it, is a DNA record, a print-out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, obviously, if it is to be admitted, then it is to be admitted under seal. We are entirely neutral about whether it is admitted at all but as I've indicated repeatedly all DNA results are agreed, and for my part I'm not sure what assistance the Trial Chamber will derive from the sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's now in the system, et cetera. It might take less time to -- to have it admitted than to further discuss on whether it should be admitted or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: D30 was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- an exhibit which Your Honours specifically asked us to focus upon to determine whether it might have closed material on it. My understanding is D30 is the set of proofing notes for Mijat Stojanovic. If that understanding is correct, there is nothing as far as we are aware in those proofing notes that requires them to be placed under seal. I think it may be that Your Honour had in mind a record of a proofing session with a witness who was a protected witness subsequently. But if D30 is as we believe it to be, the proofing notes for Mijat Stojanovic, then as far as we are aware there is nothing that requires it to be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it is a Defence exhibit although in relation to a Prosecution witness. Mr. Re, could you immediately give your position or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My understanding is Mr. Emmerson is entirely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I have not reviewed every detail of it, whether there is any information in the proofing notes which would need protection. You've carefully considered that, Mr. Emmerson?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I don't remember there being any aspect of his evidence at all that was closed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Item 5, forensic admissions. We are now in a position to provide to the Prosecution a complete response to all suggested admissions as regards the recovery of remains, the process of DNA identification, and the post-mortem findings of the international forensic pathologists. They will have that today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the next item is unofficial translations of the reports that were put by the Defence in cross-examination to Stanisa Radosevic. Your Honour asked for an update. Those documents are with the translation unit as we speak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally, there is the Prosecution's motion for a direction that there be further particulars provided by Mr. Balaj in relation to his pre-trial brief. Whilst this is an application directed to Mr. Balaj, it is one in which all parties have an interest because it proceeds from a certain assumption about what should or should not be pleaded in a pre-trial brief, and so we will want to submit our own response. We have to organise a timetable. The suggestion is three days after we return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know when you return, Mr. -- after we return to court?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm saying three days after we sit. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: After we sit. Yes. Any problem with that? Then that time-limit is accepted. Any other matter? Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just one matter and that is to facilitate these sorts of discussions about administrative matters, it would greatly assist us to get a list in advance of all these matters, and I would be able to address the Trial Chamber on the spot. When things are thrown at me about various things over the last few months, I just can't -- can't deal with them as I sit here, because it takes -- takes a while to research some of these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we've obviously -- these are all matters that have been raised in court over the last few weeks, and I'm simply drawing the threads together before we break for Easter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is the specific matter of the upcoming witness, that is Witness 21 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- with regard to any information that has been received from UNMIK, and I am at the moment limiting -- limiting the inquiry to that specific witness because I believe that individual is the next witness in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next witness is Witness 21, if I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can answer to this extent. We have received no formal response from UNMIK in relation to that particular witness. UNMIK has informed us informally that no witness statements exist in relation to the war crimes unit. There are none in UNMIK's war crimes unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in the unit crimes against humanity or unit of grave breaches? I'm -- no, I'm just wondering -- it's not a play of words, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There are -- I'm told. I'm reading from an e-mail here. There are five different units: A serious crimes unit, a war crimes unit, an investigations unit, a counter-terrorism unit, a financial crimes and economic crimes unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We have directed our inquiries across the board in relation to all of the units. The informal telephonic response we have received related to the war crimes unit, which was the most logical place to start looking. The RFA remains -- remains outstanding, we are in contact and were in contact with UNMIK by telephone today asking them to speed it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course it could be -- investigation units might be a place where you could sometimes find materials as well. But let's not -- I mean, we can't resolve the matter here at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, I don't believe we can. I notice that Mr. Re limited his remarks with regard to what he has been informally told to witness statements existing. I don't know whether or not he has received any information concerning any Rule 68 material or any other materials, and I don't want to -- I don't want to beat the horse, but I also don't want to be in a position where we are misunderstanding each other with regard to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- what is asked for. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I take it that you are able to discard any malcommunication in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We have asked UNMIK formally in an RFA, the Defence has seen it, I've shown him a copy of it or statements relating to those - whatever it was - four or five witnesses. That's what Mr. Guy-Smith requested; that is what we have asked of UNMIK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We have also informally by telephone asked an UNMIK official about statements. We do not have the information. I cannot answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's limited now until -- to two statements, from what I -- so try to resolve that --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I formally request right now that -- that he ask for Rule 68 information and for any other pertinent information that may exist in the investigator files, so there's no misunderstanding in the time that we have before this particular witness does appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that will be the request that is always made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I couldn't say that pertinent information is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is the clearest criteria. But, okay, I take it that you will communicate in such a way that the Chamber is not -- that not -- your malcommunication or misunderstandings are put to the Chamber, but the real problems that are remaining. I have full confidence that you will be able to do that. I'm addressing, of course, both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith wrote to us last week asking for that, and I have responded saying, please specify what you mean by pertinent information and what you want us to ask UNMIK. Asking us to ask UNMIK for Rule 68 material is a nebulous request; we cannot do it. I don't know what the Defence means by Rule 68. Without knowing what Mr. Balaj's defence is, it's extremely difficult for us to frame even searches within the OTP's evidence collection. So how can we possibly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not -- let's not continue. Next Tuesday if you have semantic problems with each other or even -- I'll -- although we're not sitting, everyone is welcome to come to The Hague and if need be parties can always ask for a meeting in Chambers and then you -- I can be the spectator of -- I think the message is clear. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was going to move on -- I was going to move to another issue, and that deals with the specific issue of translation of documents that specifically deal with military experts that we have yet to -- have yet to receive, and those would be translation of documents that are contained in the information of Bozidar Delic and of the information of Mr. Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And this is something that's been pending for some period of time, I just don't know what the status is of that. However, I can assure you that the information, as we understand it, is voluminous and is information that is critical for purposes of preparation for cross-examination of these military witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I take it you give Mr. Re an opportunity to check that and then to inform you by e-mail, and if need be that if the translations are not immediately available --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Those are my issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I haven't taken the complete vow of silence in relation to this case; however, I am satisfied that my colleagues have raised all of the matters that concern me, and I am very particularly concerned about the military matters that Mr. Guy-Smith has just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That request for translation has been outstanding for a long time. We were promised -- I'm sorry to prolong this. We were promised draft translations. We said we'd be very happy to accept draft translations, and we're still waiting over a month later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I notice that we are half an hour over time, which is almost impossible for interpreters and technicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have nothing of any substance to add. Simply this, we will discuss with the Prosecution immediately after court the list of witnesses that they are proposing to call after the break and ensure that the Trial Chamber is informed within the next 24 hours or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there's nothing else, then I especially would like to thank the interpreters for their -- not only for their patience but also for their hard work half an hour more than we could expect from them, same for the technicians. We will not sit next week. That means that we will - the Registrar has given it to me - we will resume at Monday, the 16th of April, quarter past 2.00, in Courtroom II. And we -- yes, this is announced in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of April, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.19 p.m.,
